limitations: LABOUR LIMIT (FR-DEV-1): developers never write programs. Every program is one of the designer's reference approaches for the task (economy.needs / usefulness tiers): a first version drawn from craft, an improvement one step up with probability craft; outcomes decide only WHEN a developer improves (retention, errors, tickets, issues), never what it writes. For a generated category the best approach implements its hidden rule, so 'novel category' services are designer code; their novelty is only that participants have no documentation for the category. Code review and pull requests recognise approaches by their exact source.

Technology invention is still inert in the DEFAULT civilisation profiles: crucible.civ.generator.ORDER has no 'devs' (CIV's file; integration note). Every Gate J/L/SP-6.3b-6.5b world is innovation.inventworld.civ_spec, the civilisation generator's own spec plus module devs, the world's generated categories (allocate, transform), the raw-feed composed activities and the configured two-step pipeline route.shortest -> pack.knapsack.

The two-step pipeline (inventworld.PIPELINE, second step 3-7 minutes against 20-45) is configured by the invention world builder: needs derived from it feed L.2-L.5 as world conditions but are not counted as SP-6.4b workflow-change examples (strict classification).

Composed activities: the raw-feed rule needs a table-producing category; with the world's two generated categories it yields exactly one composed activity (transform -> allocate). A world without a table producer has no composed activity and no workflow demand.

Seed dependence: workflows are seed dependent (creation worlds before this pass: seed 5 and 8 one verified workflow each, seeds 6 and 7 none); the civilisation gates run on one seed (balanced, seed 3); seed 4 is a factual-only robustness job in the G lane.
